key_insight: The paper presents a first-of-its-kind 1.3B-parameter generative foundation model that can synthesize and edit chest radiographs with controllable attributes and high clinical realism.
clinical_relevance: This could help expand training data, test model robustness across patient groups and imaging settings, and support safer evaluation of chest X-ray AI systems.
method: Trained from scratch at billion-parameter scale using rectified flow transformers
Used 1.6T tokens from a curated heterogeneous dataset of 1.2M radiographs plus expert-guided metadata
Enabled controllable generation across demographics, acquisition views, and multiple pathologies
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 1.2M radiographs and was reported to produce images indistinguishable from real radiographs to clinical experts.
watch_item: Synthetic radiographs may still reflect dataset biases or require careful validation before use in downstream clinical workflows.
paper_title: Scaling Generative Foundation Models for Chest Radiography with Rectified Flow Transformers
